IF YOU WANT TO PASS SYSTEM DESIGN INTERVIEWS, STOP LISTING TECHNOLOGIES.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 MOVES: 1/5

Start with requirements, not Kafka.

Users, scale, latency. Numbers first. The interviewer wants your thinking, not your stack. 2/5

Draw the happy path, then break it.

One box diagram, then ask what dies first. Bottlenecks earn more points than buzzwords. 3/5

Always close with tradeoffs.

Why this over that, and what breaks at 10x. Seniors choose and defend. 4/5

I post daily breakdowns like this for backend, SQL, and interviews.

Follow @owlsky17 so you don't miss the next one. 5/5

IF YOU WANT BEHAVIORAL ROUNDS TO REMEMBER YOU, STOP RECITING YOUR RESUME.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 STORY RULES: 1/5

One story per question, 90 seconds max.

Situation, action, result. Rambling loses the room before the result lands. 2/5

Lead with the conflict.

What was hard, who disagreed, what was at stake. Tension is what makes stories stick. 3/5

End with what you would repeat.

The lesson proves growth. Anyone can survive a mess; seniors extract the rule. 4/5

THINGS HIRING MANAGERS CAN'T TELL FROM YOUR RESUME (SO PROVE THEM IN THE INTERVIEW): 1/5

How you debug when prod is on fire.

Walk through logs, metrics, and your first three commands. Process beats claims. 2/5

Whether you unblock others.

One story about the runbook you wrote or the junior you mentored beats five teamwork bullets. 3/5

Whether your numbers are real.

p95 800ms to 480ms with one index, verified over two weeks. Specifics get interviews. 4/5
